Where · the first question

Pharma Value Chain

The drug-development pipeline as one linear chain: 3 steps and 14 substeps. Use it to anchor a course or workshop to the part of drug development it prepares people for.

3 steps · 14 substepsv0.8.0Draft: AI-drafted, pending CPDSE review

Each substep page gives the primary data-science question, the key questions teams ask at that substep, and the established methods and tools. Links to competencies come from tools listed in the crosswalk.

Step 1 Pre-clinical

  1. 1

    Disease Understanding

    What is the disease, who does it affect, and where is the unmet medical need that a new therapy could address?

    5 key questions · 6 methods and tools · 9 in the crosswalk

  2. 2

    Target Identification

    Which biological targets are most likely to be causal for the disease of interest and tractable for drug intervention?

    3 key questions · 7 methods and tools · 15 in the crosswalk

  3. 3

    Modality Selection

    Given the target and what it takes to engage it, which therapeutic modality is the right one to pursue?

    12 key questions · 5 methods and tools

  4. 4

    Lead Identification

    Which compounds from a screening library or virtual space show genuine activity against the validated target?

    3 key questions · 7 methods and tools · 18 in the crosswalkUsed in 1 example (illustrative)

  5. 5

    Lead Optimisation & Candidate Selection

    How do structural modifications improve a lead's safety, activity, selectivity, and ADMET — and which optimised compound has the best overall balance to be nominated as the development candidate?

    6 key questions · 18 methods and tools · 16 in the crosswalkUsed in 1 example (illustrative)

  6. 6

    Nonclinical Safety & DMPK

    Does the candidate have an acceptable pharmacokinetic and safety profile in preclinical models to justify first-in-human dosing?

    5 key questions · 8 methods and tools · 9 in the crosswalk

  7. 7

    Formulation & Drug Product Development (CMC)

    How do we turn the development candidate into a stable, manufacturable drug product that delivers the right exposure by the intended route?

    5 key questions · 8 methods and tools · 9 in the crosswalk

Step 2 Clinical development

  1. 8

    Biomarker Development

    Which biological markers are validated and qualified to predict treatment response or stratify patients in the clinic?

    5 key questions · 5 methods and tools · 8 in the crosswalk

  2. 9

    Clinical Pharmacology

    How does the drug behave in the body (PK) and what is the relationship between exposure and effect (PD)?

    5 key questions · 14 methods and tools · 12 in the crosswalk

  3. 10

    Phase I / II / III

    Is the drug safe, and does it produce a clinically meaningful benefit in patients at a well-defined dose?

    5 key questions · 8 methods and tools · 12 in the crosswalkUsed in 1 example (illustrative)

  4. 11

    Regulatory

    Can we assemble defensible, standards-compliant evidence that a regulator will accept to approve the drug?

    5 key questions · 5 methods and tools · 6 in the crosswalkUsed in 1 example (illustrative)

Step 3 On-market

  1. 12

    Manufacturing

    Is the manufacturing process consistent, in control, and capable of producing product within specification at scale?

    5 key questions · 7 methods and tools · 11 in the crosswalk

  2. 13

    Market Access (HEOR)

    Does the drug deliver enough value, at an acceptable cost, to justify reimbursement and adoption?

    5 key questions · 7 methods and tools · 8 in the crosswalk

  3. 14

    Pharmacovigilance & Pharmacoepidemiology

    What are the real-world safety signals and effects of the drug once it is in routine use in defined patient populations?

    5 key questions · 8 methods and tools · 18 in the crosswalk
